headline: Spatial methods tackle transcript spillover and noise-aware histology-to-expression
label: Spatial Artefacts And Histology Inference
summary: New preprints remove transcript spillover in imaging spatial data and add noise-corrected metrics and confidence to histology-based expression prediction.
synthesis: The main thread is the correction of measurement artefacts in spatial data and the reliability of molecular readouts inferred from histology. For imaging-based spatial transcriptomics, Dancer uses a reference-guided probabilistic model to separate within-cell-type heterogeneity from transcript contamination. SYNDRI removes post-segmentation spillover with a supervised transformer trained on simulated data. In histology-to-expression prediction, RSC splits RNA counts so benchmarks are scored against reproducible signal rather than noise, and REGAIN attaches per-prediction confidence before TCGA-BRCA prognostic analysis. XenoType uses paired Xenium and scRNA-seq data to supervise seven-class cell typing from H&E. VirTues-M2 jointly pretrains on H&E morphology and spatial proteomics. BioBatchNet extends disentangled batch correction to imaging mass cytometry. A secondary thread is perturbation-response modelling: the linear BiPert baseline, GAIN for combinatorial non-additive effects, the causal CMC-VAE on CITE-seq, and calibrated metrics for Virtual Cell Challenge 2026.
